A trust fund with European Investmetn Bank established and its credit programme for water/waste Water projects in 40 BiH municipalities be supported by grant money for investment and TA.

The Project concerns establishment of co-financing arrangement for municipal infrastructure projects with the European Investment Bank (EIB), with the main components: a) institutional capacity building of waste water utilities in the areas of operational efficiency and sustainability b) selective investments to the highly needed waste water treatment facilities. The overall aim of the Project is to provide improved municipal environmental infrastructure services to BiH citizens in accordance with EU directives, leading to improved environment and health. The result of the Project will be that participating municipal utilities will move towards compliance with EU-regulations on higher quality, reliability and sustainability of services, decrease environmental pollution and increase energy efficiency through a series of institutional improvements and selective investments in rehabilitation and wastewater systems. Sida contribution will be used to expand the ongoing water and sanitation programme financed from the EIB loan, EU grants and local contribution.

description.narrative:
The overview of achievements and related challenges in 2024 is presented below: Municipality of Tomislavgrad: The originally planned completion of the Waste Water Treatment Plant (WWTP) date was 31 Dec 2023. However, due to delays in the extension of the Central Supervision services contract, works were suspended from Sept 2023 until June 30, 2024. These delays have financial implications on the Contractor and caused serious contractual issues, which were overcame after negotiations. Due to the described delays and contractual disputes, it is expected that the works can be completed by 30 June 2025, upon signing of the Annex of the Contract. Municipality of Bosanski Petrovac: The implementation of the works on WWTP also suffered delays due to the unavailability of the Supervising Engineer. These delays also caused of additional claims by the contractor due to the suspension of work for about 12 months. This administrative procedure is subject of negotiations between Contractor and the Municipality. Central Supervision held several meetings with representatives of the contractor, and the municipality, and consequently submitted proposal to the Municipality regarding the additional claims by the contractor. Following the acceptance of the claim by the Municipality, works can resume and completion is foreseen by December 2025. Mostar: Works on Waste Water infrastructure dully completed in 2022 Municipality of Trebinje: The WWTP is completed, including the procurement and installation of the additional sludge treatment equipment which was finalized in June 2024 Municipality of Teslic: The WWTP works are fully completed in 2023
Generally, key challenge during past year was the delayed extension of the Contract for Supervision Services (pending long term ratification process) which consequently caused further delays in implementation in FBIH. The contract between the Federal Ministry of Agriculture Water Management and Forestry and the Supervising Engineer was renewed in July 2024 after almost 12 month of supervision suspension. These delays created additional financial claims by some contractors, requiring additional negotiations and creating further delays and financial burden on some municipalities. Given the further delays in the execution in two municipalities, yet another no-cost extension is necessary. In July 2024, EIB submitted no-cost extension request which consequently have been approved. The contribution will be extended until February 2027.
